qa_pairs.instruction: Summarize how to display the driver shim status for the Bi Impl Scripting driver on all supported operating systems.
qa_pairs.output:
To display the driver shim status for the Bi Impl Scripting driver, run the appropriate command for your platform: 
- AIX: `/etc/rc.d/init.d/usdrvd status`
- FreeBSD: `/usr/local/etc/rc.d/usdrvd status`
- HP-UX: `/sbin/init.d/usdrvd status`
- Linux: `/etc/init.d/usdrvd status`
- macOS (OSX): `/opt/novell/usdrv/startup/usdrvd status`
- Solaris: `/etc/init.d/usdrvd status`
- Tru64: `/etc/init.d/usdrvd status`
- Windows: use the Windows Services application to view the service status.

qa_pairs.instruction: How do you check the driver shim status for the Bi Impl Scripting driver on a Linux system?
qa_pairs.output: On a Linux system, open a terminal with appropriate privileges and run the command `/etc/init.d/usdrvd status`. The output will show the current status and version information of the Bi Impl Scripting driver shim.

qa_pairs.instruction: How can you view the Bi Impl Scripting driver shim status on a Windows machine?
qa_pairs.output: On Windows, open the Windows Services application (services.msc), locate the service named "usdrvd" (or the Bi Impl Scripting driver shim service), and check its status column. This displays whether the driver shim is running and its version information.

qa_pairs.instruction: What command should you use to display the Bi Impl Scripting driver shim status on an AIX server?
qa_pairs.output: On AIX, execute the command `/etc/rc.d/init.d/usdrvd status` from a shell with sufficient privileges. The command returns the status and version details of the Bi Impl Scripting driver shim.
